note: THE category-exclude LIBRARY - single source of truth for wrong-class product tokens. Three consumers: (1) audit-food-category.ps1 (blocking guard: a food commodity matched to one of these classes hard-fails the publish), (2) apply-category-excludes.ps1 (bakes these patterns into every commodity's exclude list by category, so NEW commodities are born with the guardrails), (3) build-vet-sheet.ps1 (flags them for batch review). Born from the 2026-07-14 blueberries-as-Bai-beverage live mispricing. RULE FOR ADDING PATTERNS: a token belongs here ONLY if it is wrong for EVERY commodity in the scoped categories (after exempt); anything item-specific stays in that commodity's own exclude list. frozen_dessert_brand (2026-08-30, queue 2026-08-30-2611d3) is the first BRAND class: Blue Bunny crowned Family Fare pistachios at $0.1248/oz with a 48 oz tub of ice cream, and every type-word fence missed it because the retail name carries only BRAND + FLAVOR (no ice cream, no dessert, no frozen). A brand token only belongs here when every product the brand sells is the wrong class: all 40 Blue Bunny strings in out/ are frozen desserts, and the exempt regex carries the commodities a Blue Bunny product legitimately IS. sausage_carrier (2026-09-02, queue 2026-09-02-1527d2) is the first CARRIER-FORM class: a chicken sausage flavoured with gruyere held the Family Fare gruyere cell at $0.5825/oz, and nothing in a library of brand and type words could say that a product is a sausage which lists the food as a flavour. Measured the same day over 33,854 corpus names: 455 carry sausage(s) and 25 of those route to 15 commodities that are not sausage (apples five times over), a gap that had been closed one per-product ruling at a time since 2026-08-01. The exempt regex carries the 21 ids that ARE a sausage or legitimately contain one; a sausage is the wrong product for every other commodity in the scoped categories, which is what makes this a library class rather than 15 separate excludes. cheese_carrier and cracker_carrier (2026-09-04, queue 2026-09-04-2cd17a, triage-plans\plan-2026-09-04.json) are the same shape one category further out: Aldi's 'Emporium Selection Bacon Bread Cheese 6 OZ' (a baked CHEESE) routed to bacon and its Original sibling to bread, and 'Savoritz Sea Salt Sourdough Pita Cracker 5 OZ' routed to pita-bread because that commodity's hand-written exclude carried the literal plural 'crackers' and the singular walked past it - the library already had the \bcrackers?\b form in snack_carrier but no bake scope reached Bread & Bakery. Bread & Bakery gets its own apply block for that reason (it previously shared the Dairy/Canned/... block and therefore could not gain a class the others must not have).

apply.note: Bread & Bakery used to fall into the shared Dairy/Canned/Sauces/... block below and therefore could not be given a class the others must not have. This block MUST stay above that one: apply-category-excludes.ps1:34 takes the FIRST block whose regex matches the category label, so a block appended after the shared one would be unreachable (the first-match-wins trap that left dried_carrier baked into 0 of 83 vegetables). Its first eight classes are exactly the shared block's; the last two are what Bread gains.

dried/flake spice-jar forms are wrong for every FRESH-produce commodity, but Fruit is excluded from scope on purpose: dried-cranberries and raisins are Fruit rows whose own products carry the word dried. Born from the 2026-08-20 contested review: Dan's Pantry Rosemary, Gourmet Garden basil paste, freeze-dried red onion and McCormick celery flakes were all pricing fresh rows.
